A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaintainCoder and MaintainBench. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the relocated checklist and original case study.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations and robustness experiments in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds human and model comparisons, computational-cost results and a qualitative application case study.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A retain the same agents, architectural-design and code-generation modules, refinement loops and prompts. The o3-mini evaluation and MVC application example do not document a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The five MaintainBench datasets remain unchanged. Appendix F adds a qualitative 2048-game generation and maintenance scenario involving high-contrast colors and a tile-feature modification, modestly extending application coverage. SWE-Bench is mentioned only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 5 substantially expands comparison coverage with human programmers, o3-mini, EvoMAC using GPT-4o-mini, and MetaGPT using GPT-4.1-mini. Existing comparators remain. Table 6 additionally includes a combined MetaGPT/ChatDev entry for token costs; ChatDev does not receive maintainability scores.

E3.justification: The added human comparison specifies Codeforces ratings of 1700–2300 and 30 minutes per problem. New evaluations use o3-mini and a GPT-4.1-mini backbone for MetaGPT, and introduce token usage as an evaluation measure. Existing benchmark sampling, preprocessing and two-phase generation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds computational-cost analysis and stage-level token accounting in Tables 6 and 9, plus a qualitative MVC case study describing localization of requirement changes. Existing component ablations, Pass@k robustness curves, alternative Phase II generator results and the cyclic-array example are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains five-round averaging and the same Pass@k reporting practice. The new comparisons introduce no additional seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New comparison and resource-use results substantially extend the reported findings. Table 5 newly reports CodeContests-Dyn Pass@5 of 36.4% for MaintainCoder with o3-mini, 30.3% for o3-mini and 23.5% for human-programmer code. Table 6 adds MaintainCoder token totals of 33.1k on CodeContests and 29.6k on xCodeEval, with a breakdown in Table 9. Original numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The discounted maintenance-cost definition, Monte Carlo and first-order approximation, and benchmark-construction equations are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v3 adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, engineering-based multi-agent contribution, maintainability improvements exceeding 60%, improved initial correctness and preference for dynamic metrics. New experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning human performance under time pressure, upfront computational cost versus later maintenance savings, and MVC-based localization of changes. The conclusion explicitly proposes repository-level evaluation such as SWE-Bench, replacing v2's future direction of reducing inflated code length.

D1.justification: v3 provides an explicit repository resource URL where v2 points to anonymous supplementary materials, and adds stage-level token accounting in Table 9. Appendix D retains temperature 0.3, top-p 0.95, iteration limits and metric-computation details.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to ChatDev, EvoMAC and Zhang et al.'s survey, with brief accompanying additions in Sections 1–2. The broader positioning around neglected maintainability and the value of software-engineering principles remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands the discussion, adds a structured 2048 case study and acknowledgements, revises the conclusion and publication header, moves the checklist before the appendices, and makes the existing toy example Appendix G. Most original scientific prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5, 6 and 9 and a repository-directory display. Existing tables and all seven figures are preserved; v2's appendix Tables 5 and 6 become Tables 7 and 8. Layout changes mainly involve local reflow, relocated material and code-listing styling.

improvement.justification: The new comparisons and token accounting in Tables 5, 6 and 9 improve assessment of competitiveness and computational overhead, while the explicit resource link improves documentation. These gains are limited: the human evaluation omits participant counts, claimed human maintenance-effort savings are not directly measured, and the 2048 example remains qualitative. The core method and original experimental evidence are unchanged.
